content: Set r(x)=p(x)-x. Then p(p(x))-x=r(x)+r(x+r(x)). Exact binomial expansion gives r(x+r(x))=r(x)+r'(x)r(x)+r(x)^2s(x), hence the target condition for nonzero r implies r divides 2+r'. If r is nonconstant, degree comparison forces 2+r'=0, so r=-2x+c and p=-x+c. If r is a nonzero constant c, then p=x+c; r=0 gives p=x. Converse witnesses: q=2/c for p=x+c with c nonzero, and q=0 for p=x or p=-x+c. No external theorem is needed.
